Copy from Daily Report of Officer in charge of Dixwell Road Police Station.
Thursday, 4th. March 1937.

PATROL
(PARTY VAN)
No.38
Between 3 and 7.p.m. 3-3-37, a Radio Van patrolled Dixwell
Road and Kashing Road districts. No searching done in the
Dixwell Road district and no reports.

CEREMONY
AT THE
SHO KONSHA
SHRINE.
A memorial service for those who fell in the 1932 Shanghai
Incident was held at the Japanese Shrine, Kungwen Road,
between 10.30.a.m. and 12.30.p.m. 3-3-37. The ceremony
was attended by diplomatic, consular, military and naval
officials and various representatives of the Japanese
community. Consular police were in attendance inside the
shrine and the necessary precautionary measures taken by
officers from this station. S.C. "E" attended.
During the afternoon visits and other contacts were
carried, the programme concluding at 4.30.p.m. No untoward
incidents.

1937年3月4日，星期四。

巡逻
（警车组）
第38号
1937年3月3日下午3时至7时，一辆无线电警车在迪克斯威尔路（Dixwell Road）和嘉善路（Kashing Road）地区巡逻。未在迪克斯威尔路地区进行搜查，亦无报告。

招魂社
神社
仪式。
1937年3月3日上午10时30分至下午12时30分，在虹口路（Kungwen Road）日本神社举行了纪念1932年上海事变中阵亡者的追悼会。外交、领事、军事和海军官员以及日本侨民界的各种代表出席了仪式。领事警察在神社内执勤，本巡捕房的警官采取了必要的预防措施。特别处“E”股出席。
下午进行了拜访和其他接触，活动于下午4时30分结束。未发生异常事件。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
Misc File No. 19/36
Dixwell Road Station,
REPORT
Date March 3, 19 36

Subject The Annual Festival of the Shokonsha held at the Japanese Shrine,
Kiangwan Road, between 10 a.m. and 11 a.m. 3-3-36.

Made by D.S.I. McPhee Forwarded by

Sir,
A ceremony in connection with the Annual Festival of the
Shokonsha was held in the Japanese Shrine, Kiangwan Road, between
10 a.m. and 11 a.m. 3-3-36.
The following persons were amongst those who attended the
ceremony :-
The Japanese Ambassador to China Mr. H. Arita, Consul
General Mr. I. Ishii, Vice Admiral Oikawa, Commander in Chief
of the Third Fleet, Rear Admiral Kondo, Commander Japanese Naval
Landing Party, Rear Admiral Soto Naval Attache, Major General
Isoya Military Attache, and representatives of the various
Japanese community organisations in Shanghai.
Mr. A. Tajima (D.C. of Police) and Capt. E.R. Kennedy, D.O.
"C" Division, were in attendance.
Between 1.30 p.m. and 4 p.m. 3-3-36, various entertainments
were staged in the compound at the Shrine.
Members of the Uniform Branch and Crime Branch from Dixwell
Road, Kashing Road, Hongkew, West Hongkew, Reserve Unit and
Special Branch, under Inspector Eva, i/c Dixwell Road, were on
duty in the vicinity of the Shrine.
Japanese Consular Police and members of the Naval Landing
Party were on duty inside the Shrine.
Nothing untoward occurred during the day's proceedings.

I am, Sir,
Yours obediently,
John McPhee
D. S. I.

D. D. O. "C"
Jle
Mg
4 MAR. 1936

主题 1936年3月3日上午10时至11时在江湾路（Kiangwan Road）日本神社举行的招魂社年度祭典。

由特别处副总督察 McPhee 撰写，呈报人

先生，
1936年3月3日上午10时至11时，在江湾路日本神社举行了与招魂社年度祭典相关的仪式。
出席仪式的人员包括：-
日本驻华大使有田八郎（H. Arita）先生，总领事石射猪太郎（I. Ishii）先生，第三舰队司令长官及川古志郎（Oikawa）海军中将，日本海军陆战队指挥官近藤英次郎（Kondo）海军少将，海军武官佐藤（Soto）海军少将，陆军武官矶谷（Isoya）陆军少将，以及上海各日本侨民团体的代表。
警察局副局长 Tajima（A. Tajima）先生和“C”分区行动警官 Kennedy（E.R. Kennedy）上尉出席了活动。
1936年3月3日下午1时30分至4时，在神社院内上演了各种娱乐节目。
在迪克斯威尔路主管警官 Eva 督察的指挥下，来自迪克斯威尔路、嘉善路、虹口、西虹口、后备队及特别处的制服部和刑事部成员在神社附近执勤。
日本领事警察和日本海军陆战队成员在神社内部执勤。
当天的活动中未发生任何异常事件。

此致，
敬礼，
John McPhee
特别处副总督察

“C”分区副行动警官
Jle
Mg
1936年3月4日

REPORT
Date: February 24, 1936

Subject The Annual Festival of the Shokonsha to be held at the Shanghai
Jinsha Shrine on March 3.

Made by D.S.I. Umemoto Forwarded by

A ceremony in connection with the annual festival of the
Shokonsha will be held at the Shanghai Jinsha Shrine, Kiangwan
Road, at 10.30 a.m. March 3. The function will last about one
hour. Vice-Admiral Oikawa, Commander-in-Chief of the Third Fleet,
Rear-Admirals Kondo and Sato, Mr. Ishii, Consul-General, and
representatives from various public bodies and institutions are
expected to attend.

Performances will be staged in the compound of the shrine
from 2 p.m. to about 4 p.m.

In order to consider precautionary measures to be adopted
on the occasion, members of the Japanese Consular Police, the
Japanese Residents' Corporation and other bodies held a meeting
at the Japanese Club between 1 p.m. and 2 p.m. February 28.

It was decided that the Consular Police be detailed for
duty at the shrine from 9.30 a.m. until the termination of the
various functions; that members of other organizations also assist
in maintaining order inside the compound.

The Committee formed in connection with the ceremony will
request the co-operation of the Municipal Police in regulating
traffic on Kiangwan Road and the maintenance of order in the
vicinity.

Details of men from Sp. Br.
who will attend will
be forwarded on Mar 2.
HG
D. S. I.
（签名：Umemoto）

Deputy Commissioner, Special Branch.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
S. 2, Special Branch.
REPORT
Date. February 28, 1935.

Subject Annual Memorial Service of the Shokonsha Shrine to be held
on March 3, 1935.

Made by D. S. Umemoto. Forwarded by.

The annual Grand Memorial Service for the Japanese who
fell during the Sino-Japanese hostilities in Shanghai in 1932
will be held by the Japanese community at the Shanghai Shrine,
Kiangwan Road, on March 3, 1935. The service will commence
at 10.00 a.m. and will last about one and a half hours. Many
Japanese notables including Mr. Ariyoshi, Minister to China,
Mr. Ishii, Consul-General, Lieutenant-General Suzuki, Military
Attache, Rear-Admiral Sato, Naval Attache, Rear Admiral Araki,
Commander of the Japanese Naval Landing Party, will attend the
function. Representatives of the following bodies will also
be present during the ceremony:-
Japanese Naval Landing Party
Japanese Ex-Service Men's Association
Japanese Schools
Japanese Street Unions
Japanese Company, S.V.C.

In addition to the service the following exhibitions will
be held in honour of the occasion:-
Wrestling Bouts will be held at 1.00 p.m. in the compound
of the former Headquarters of the Japanese Naval Landing Party,
north end of Darroch Road.
Fencing and Bayonet Fighting will be carried out in the
compound of the shrine from 1.00 p.m. to 4.00 p.m.
Between 1 p.m. and 2.30 p.m., February 27, a meeting was
held by some 18 members of the Policing Committee at the
Japanese Club, Boone Road, to discuss measures to be adopted
in providing necessary protection at the shrine and its
vicinity on March 3 on the occasion of the service.
The following decisions were reached:-

主题 1935年3月3日将举行的招魂社年度追悼会。

由特别处侦探 Umemoto 撰写。呈报人。

日本侨民界将于1935年3月3日在江湾路上海神社为1932年中日冲突中阵亡的日本人举行年度大追悼会。仪式将于上午10时开始，持续约一个半小时。许多日本名流将出席该活动，包括驻华公使有吉明（Ariyoshi）先生，总领事石井（Ishii）先生，陆军武官铃木（Suzuki）中将，海军武官佐藤（Sato）海军少将，日本海军陆战队指挥官荒木（Araki）海军少将。以下团体的代表也将在仪式期间出席：-
日本海军陆战队
日本退伍军人协会
日本学校
日本街道联合会
上海义勇队日本连

除仪式外，还将举行以下展览以资纪念：-
下午1时，将在达罗克路（Darroch Road）北端原日本海军陆战队总部院内举行摔跤比赛。
下午1时至4时，将在神社院内举行击剑和刺刀格斗表演。
2月27日下午1时至2时30分，约18名警务委员会成员在布恩路（Boone Road）日本俱乐部举行会议，讨论3月3日仪式期间在神社及其附近提供必要保护措施的事宜。

Sir,
Information has been received by J.D.C. 32 Hara from the
Japanese Naval Landing Party Headquarter, Kiangwan Road, to the
effect that a Memorial Service in honour of the Japanese
combatants killed in the Sino-Japanese conflict of 1932 in
Shanghai, will be held at the Shanghai Shrine, Kiangwan Road, on
the 3rd. March 1934, commencing at 9.00 a.m.
It is stated that the Japanese Consul General, Mr. Ishii,
Vice-Admiral Namura, Rear Admiral Uno and Staff will be in
attendance, together with one company detailed from the Japanese
Naval Landing Party, details from the Japanese Company, S.V.C.,
and representatives of the divers Japanese communal organisations
in Shanghai.
In the afternoon of the same date, various entertainments
will be staged at the shrine, and premises adjacent to the
Japanese Naval Landing Party Headquarters, which was previously
utilised as barracks.

I am, Sir,

Subject (in full) Service in memory of Japanese who fell during the Sino-Japanese hostilities in Shanghai in 1932 to be held on March 3.
Made by D. S. Umemoto. Forwarded by A. O. Burnett

At 1 p.m. February 28, a meeting of members of the Order Maintenance Committee in connection with the memorial service for all Japanese who fell during the Sino-Japanese hostilities in Shanghai in 1932 was held in the Japanese Residents Corporation, Quinsan Road. Mr. Hamato, Chief of the Consular Police Station, presided over the function.

It was decided that all the parties who are to police the ceremonial ground and its vicinity are to take up their posts at 9 a.m. March 3.

The service will commence at 10 a.m. and will last about 1½ hours. The proceedings will be attended by Mr. Ariyoshi, Japanese Minister to China, Mr. Ishii, Japanese Consul General, Vice Admiral Imamura, Commander-in-Chief of the Third Fleet, Major General Suzuki, Military Attaché, Rear Admiral Sugisaka, Commander of the 11th Squadron, Rear Admiral Uno, Commander of the Naval Landing Party, and many other officials and prominent residents. Representatives of various Japanese institutions and public bodies will also attend.

After the service exhibition of fencing and bayonet fighting will be staged in the compound of the Shanghai Jinsha Shrine, Kiangwan Road. Wrestling bouts will be carried out in the compound of the former headquarters of the Japanese Naval Landing Party, corner of North Szechuen Road and Darroch Road. It is expected that the exhibitions will last till late in the afternoon.

D. S. Umemoto
D. S.
Deputy Commissioner,
Special Branch.

2月28日下午1时，在昆山路日本居留民团举行了维持秩序委员会成员会议，商讨为所有在1932年上海中日冲突中阵亡的日本人举行即将召开的追悼会事宜。领事警察署署长滨户（Hamato）先生主持了该活动。

会议决定，所有负责警戒仪式现场及其周边的各方人员须于3月3日上午9时到岗。

仪式将于上午10时开始，持续约1个半小时。有吉明日本驻华公使、石井日本总领事、第三舰队司令长官今村中将、铃木武官少将、第11战队司令杉坂少将、海军陆战队司令宇野少将以及许多其他官员和知名居民将出席仪式。各日本机构和公共团体的代表也将出席。

仪式结束后，将在江湾路上海金砂神社校园内举行击剑和刺刀格斗表演。摔跤比赛将在前日本海军陆战队总部校园内举行，地点位于北四川路与达罗克路（Darroch Road）转角。预计表演将持续至下午晚些时候。

Made by .................... and ................................ Forwarded by Inspector Jefferson.

Sir,
I respectfully beg to report that following a three-day
celebration the annual festival of the Japanese Shanghai Jinja,
Shinto Shrine, which commenced on the 1st. and continued on the
2nd. and 3rd. November 1936, was concluded at 9.0.p.m. 3-11-36.
Commencing with a flag raising ceremony at 7.30.a.m. on the
1-11-36, and from 10.30.a.m. to 11.30.a.m. daily with religious
ceremonies, and a religious ceremony on the 3-11-36, until 12.0
Noon, when the following notables attended:-
Mr. Fukui, Consul,
Vice Admiral Oikawa and staff,
Rear Admiral Konda and staff,
Mr. Amano, Chairman of the Japanese Residents
Corporation, and other Japanese notables attended.
Festivities were carried on throughout the day on the
3 days from 1.0.p.m. to 8.30.p.m., and a cinema show was given
each evening from 7.0.p.m. to 9.0.p.m., showing the Japanese
Olympic team at the Berlin games. On the 3-11-36, during the
whole day it was estimated that about 10,000 Japanese residents
attended the shrine.
During the whole 3 days there was nothing of an untoward
nature happened and no obstruction to traffic occurred.
Between the hours of 10.30.a.m. to 12 Noon on the 3-11-36,
the C.G. Omnibusses turned at North Szechuen, Darroch Roads this
was during the time of the religious ceremony by previous arrange-
ments with the Asst. Traffic Manager of the Bus Company, and
Officer i/c D.Rd.
At 1.30.p.m. on the 3-11-36, a procession of between
70-80 Japanese "Geisha" girls proceeded from the Kabukiza

PRESS INFORMATION OF ICR
Oct. 27, 1936.

ANNUAL FESTIVAL OF JAPANESE SHRINE
----------------------------------

According to the Japanese press, as one of the important
Japanese functions here, the annual festival of the Japanese
shrine in Kiangwan Road will be observed by the Japanese community
on three successive days, viz. November 1, 2 and 3. At a meeting
held yesterday at the Japanese Residents' Corporation, represen-
tatives of the Japanese Consulate-General and various other organi-
sations, and two Japanese officers from the S.M.V. discussed
traffic arrangements on the festival days, deciding tentatively
as follows:-

"(1). During the ceremony on November 3 vehicular traffic
shall be prohibited in a section of Kiangwan road marked out in
the south by a line between the watch-tower of the Landing Party
and the Public School building, and in the north by a line between
the omnibus terminus and the Junior Golf Club building in
Hongkew Park.

"(2). On November 1 and 2 traffic shall be closed in
principle for vehicles, but this arrangement may be modified
according to the situation.

"(3). The parking place for stationary buses shall be
set out on a side of Hongkew Park, but one each of No. 1, 2 and
6 routes buses may be parked on the north side of the back
gate of the shrine. In the morning of November 3, however,
north-bound buses shall not be allowed to proceed beyond a Japanese
temple called Chien-in at the North intersection of Darroch Road
and North Szechuen Road.

"(4). On the three festival days motor cars coming to the
shrine shall be stopped in front of the gasoline standard
opposite the shrine and parked in front of Hongkew Park.

"(5). Competent persons shall be detailed by the Japanese
Consulate-General and the Residents' Corporation for the guidance

据日本报刊报道，作为此处重要的日本活动之一，江湾路日本神社的年度大祭将由日本社区连续三天，即11月1日、2日和3日举行。昨日在日本居留民团举行的会议上，日本总领事馆代表、各其他组织代表以及两名来自上海志愿队（S.M.V.）的日本军官讨论了节日期间的交通安排，初步决定如下：

“(1). 11月3日举行仪式期间，江湾路的一段路段将禁止车辆通行，该路段南界为陆战队瞭望塔与公立学校大楼之间的连线，北界为公共汽车终点站与虹口公园少年高尔夫俱乐部大楼之间的连线。

“(2). 11月1日和2日原则上禁止车辆通行，但可根据实际情况修改此安排。

“(3). 静止公共汽车的停车场设在虹口公园一侧，但1路、2路和6路公共汽车可各有一辆停放在神社后门北侧。然而，在11月3日上午，北行公共汽车不得越过达罗克路与北四川路交叉口北侧的一座名为“千音”（Chien-in，音译）的日本寺庙。

“(4). 在这三个节日里，前往神社的汽车应在神社对面的汽油标准柱前停下，并停放在虹口公园前。

“(5). 日本总领事馆和居留民团将指派专人指导

Made by D.S.I. Umemoto. Forwarded by (签名)
The Autumn Grand Festival of the Shanghai Shrine will be
observed on the shrine premises on Kiangwan Road on November
1, 2 and 3, 1936.
Between 1.00 p.m. and 3.30 p.m. October 26, a meeting
was held at the Japanese Residents' Corporation by some 20
representatives of the Japanese Consular Police, the Japanese
Naval Landing Party, the Japanese Gendarmerie, the Japanese
Ex-Service Men's Association, the Japanese Company, S.V.C.,
the Japanese Residents' Corporation and the Shanghai Shrine,
to consider measures to be adopted in providing protection at
the shrine and its vicinity during the Festival.
The following decisions were reached:-
1) Policing of areas surrounding the shrine and the regulation
of traffic will be undertaken by the Municipal Police.
2) Precautions within the compound of the shrine will be
controlled by the Japanese Consular Police.
3) The Japanese Naval Landing Party will adopt precautionary
measures in the vicinity of the shrine on the morning of
November 3 when a special religious ceremony will be observed.
4) Precautionary measures will be adopted from 9.30 a.m. until
the termination of the various functions on each day.
5) Precautions at the Rifle Range adjoining the shrine will be
controlled by the Russian Unit, S.V.C., stationed at the Rifle
Range. In this connection, a request will be made to the
S.V.C. through the Japanese Company, S.V.C.
6) The Japanese Residents' Corporation will issue special
badges to newspaper reporters and photographers.

Copy from Daily Report of Officer in charge of Dixwell Road Police Station.
Monday, 4 / 11 / 35.

FESTIVITIES:
SHANGHAI
JAPANESE
SHRINE KIANG-
WAN ROAD.

The Annual three day festival of the Japanese Shanghai
Shrine on the Kiangwan Road commenced at 9.30.a.m. 1-11-35
and concluded at 8.45.p.m. 3-11-35. The festivities con-
sisted of religious ceremonies in the forenoon and amateur
theatricals and cinematograph shows in the afternoon and
evenings. Large numbers of Japanese residents attended the
various functions at the Shrine and at an all day athletic
meeting which was held in connection with the festivities at
Hongkew Park on the 3-11-35. The Japanese Ambassador, Mr.
Ariyoshi and Consul General Ishi attended the religious
ceremony on the forenoon of the 3-11-35.

Between 10.10 and 11.50.a.m. 3-11-35, Kiangwan Road,
between the Public School for Boys and the North junction of
North Szechuan and Kiangwan Road was closed to all vehicular
traffic with the exception of cars with special passes issued
to official visitors to the Shrine.

During the period of the festivities the staff of the
Station was augmented, through arrangements made by the
S.M.P., by details of foreign and Japanese police from the
Reserve Unit and Yuching Road Station and detectives from
Hongkew Station. Detectives from the Special Branch were also
in attendance.

No untoward incident occurred.

October 25, 1935. Morning Translation.

NICHI-NICHI

FIVE JAPANESE ARRESTED BY JAPANESE CONSULAR
POLICE.

At 4.30 p.m. yesterday the
Japanese Consular Police arrested five Japanese at
the Kiyo Kwan Hotel on Darroch Road on suspicion of
being concerned with smuggling. It is reported
that they were planning a serious plot.

NIPPO

POLICE MEASURES ON THE OCCASION OF SHANGHAI
SHRINE FESTIVITY.

As a result of the conference
held by the Japanese Landing Party, Consular authorities
and the S.M.P. authorities regarding the police
measures to be taken on the occasion of the Shanghai
Shrine Festivity which will be held for three days as
from November 1, the following matters were decided:-
1. That no vehicles be allowed to travel on the
part of Kiangwen Road from the front of the Japanese
Landing Party Headquarters to the entrance of Hongkew
Park between 10 a.m. to noon for three days as from
November 1.
2. That private cars belonging to the attendants
at the festivity be parked in front of Hongkew Park.
3. That the Buses turn in front of the Swimming
Bath(at the corner of North Szechuen and Darroch Roads)
4. That cattle be forbidden to enter the Shrine
compound.
5. That all pilgrims be advised to wear either
European clothing or Japanese dress in order to assist
the police officers in distinguishing them from others.
6. That persons attending the festivity in groups
be forbidden to carry banners and other cumbersome
articles.
7. That the newspaper reporters and cameramen
be given armlets by the Japanese Residents Corporation.
8. That all the pilgrims be subjected to a
search by the police if required.

五名日本人被日本领事警察逮捕。

《日本日报》

上海神社祭典期间的警务措施。

鉴于日本海军陆战队、领事当局与工部局警务处（S.M.P.）当局就将于11月1日起为期三天的上海神社祭典期间所采取的警务措施举行了会议，决定如下事项：-
1. 自11月1日起的三天内，每天上午10时至中午12时，禁止车辆在江湾路（Kiangwen Road）从日本海军陆战队总部门前至虹口公园入口路段行驶。
2. 参加祭典人员的私家车须停放在虹口公园门前。
3. 公共汽车须在游泳池前（北四川路与达罗路转角处）掉头。
4. 禁止牛只进入神社大院。
5. 建议所有参拜者穿着欧式服装或日式服装，以便警务人员将其与其他人区分开来。
6. 禁止成群参加祭典的人员携带旗帜及其他笨重物品。
7. 由日本居留民团向报社记者和摄影师发放臂章。
8. 如有需要，所有参拜者均须接受警方搜查。

（批注：D.C.(Dr) / Joseph D.O.C / case upon / -c? / AB / 1935年10月25日 / D.O.C / 请照办。Rcy / 25/10）

October 25, 1935. Morning Translation

NICHI-NICHI

FIVE JAPANESE ARRESTED BY JAPANESE CONSULAR
POLICE.

At 4.30 p.m. yesterday the
Japanese Consular Police arrested five Japanese at
the Kiyo Kwan Hotel on Darroch Road on suspicion of
being concerned with smuggling. It is reported
that they were planning a serious plot.

NIPPO

POLICE MEASURES ON THE OCCASION OF SHANGHAI
SHRINE FESTIVITY.

As a result of the conference
held by the Japanese Landing Party, Consular authorities
and the S.M.P. authorities regarding the police
measures to be taken on the occasion of the Shanghai
Shrine Festivity which will be held for three days as
from November 1, the following matters were decided:-
1. That no vehicles be allowed to travel on the
part of Kiangwan Road from the front of the Japanese
Landing Party Headquarters to the entrance of Hongkew
Park between 10 a.m. to noon for three days as from
November 1.
2. That private cars belonging to the attendants
at the festivity be parked in front of Hongkow Park.
3. That the Buses turn in front of the Swimming
Bath(at the corner of North Szechuen and Darroch Roads)
4. That cattle be forbidden to enter the Shrine
compound.
5. That all pilgrims be advised to wear either
European clothing or Japanese dress in order to assist
the police officers in distinguishing them from others.
6. That persons attending the festivity in groups
be forbidden to carry banners and other cumbersome
articles.
7. That the newspaper reporters and cameramen
be given armlts by the Japanese Residents Corporation.
8. That all the pilgrims be subjected to a
search by the police if required.

1935年10月25日。晨间译件

《日日新闻》

五名日本人被日本领事警察逮捕。

昨日下午4时30分，日本领事警察在达罗路（Darroch Road）的纪阳馆酒店（Kiyo Kwan Hotel）逮捕了五名日本人，涉嫌参与走私活动。据报，他们正策划一起严重的阴谋。

《日本日报》

上海神社祭典期间的警务措施。

鉴于日本海军陆战队、领事当局与工部局警务处（S.M.P.）当局就将于11月1日起为期三天的上海神社祭典期间所采取的警务措施举行了会议，决定如下事项：-
1. 自11月1日起的三天内，每天上午10时至中午12时，禁止车辆在江湾路（Kiangwan Road）从日本海军陆战队总部门前至虹口公园入口路段行驶。
2. 参加祭典人员的私家车须停放在虹口公园（Hongkow Park）门前。
3. 公共汽车须在游泳池前（北四川路与达罗路转角处）掉头。
4. 禁止牛只进入神社大院。
5. 建议所有参拜者穿着欧式服装或日式服装，以便警务人员将其与其他人区分开来。
6. 禁止成群参加祭典的人员携带旗帜及其他笨重物品。
7. 由日本居留民团向报社记者和摄影师发放臂章（armlts）。
8. 如有需要，所有参拜者均须接受警方搜查。

Sir,

From 10.30.a.m to 12 noon 3.11.34 ceremonial rites were held
at the Shanghai Shrine during which Mr Ariyoshi Minister to
China, Mr Ishi Consul General, Vice Admiral Imamura Commander in-
chief of the Third Fleet, Vice Admiral Uno Commander of the
Japanese Landing Party attended.

Between 1.p.m. and 4.15.p.m. Japanese Naval Sports were held
in the Hongkew Park when Vice Admiral Imamura and Vice Admiral
Uno were in attendance.

A series of entertainments took place during the hours of
3.p.m. until 5.30.p.m. in the compound of the Shrine.

From 7.p.m. to 8.30.p.m. a cinema show took place.

Throughout the above hours there was a very large attendance
of the Japanese community, both at the Shrine and Hongkew Park.

Under the Officer in charge of this district, three Japanese
detectives from Hongkew Station, one from Wayside Station, one from
Yulin Road Station, members of the Special Branch, two foreigners
from Hongkew Station, and a party of Police from Reserve Unit (B)
in conjunction with the Japanese Consular Police functioned in the
locality.

No untoward incident occurred.

I am, Sir,

Subject (in full) Festival of the Shanghai Jinsha Shrine held on November 3.

Made by D. S. Umimoto. Forwarded by A. D. Sovernal.

The following programme was carried out on November 3, the third and last day of the grand festival in connection with the Shanghai Jinsha Shrine:-

9.00 a.m. to 10.30 a.m.
Various Shinto ceremonies were solemnized at the shrine. Mr. Ishii, Japanese Consula-General, and Vice-Aimiral Imamura, Commander-in-Chief of the Japanese Third Fleet, officially called to pay their respects.

12.30 p.m. to 3.40 p.m.
Classical and modern dances were staged at the shrine.

1.40 p.m. to 1.55 p.m.
A procession of some 30 geisha girls in special designed robes was held on Kiangwan Road.

1.30 p.m. to 4.20 p.m.
Bicycle races were carried out in Hongkew Park.

1.00 p.m. to 5.20 p.m.
Wrestling bouts took place on the Japanese Naval Ground, North Szechuen Road.

7.00 p.m. to 8.30 p.m.
An exhibition of cinema films was given at the shrine.

The day being the anniversary of the birthday of the late Emperor Meiji, most of the Japanese firms and shops were closed, and some 10,000 persons turned up to attend the ceremonies.

Special precautionary measures were enforced by Police Officers from Dixwell and Kashing Road Stations and the Reserve Unit in conjunction with the local Japanese Consular Police.

D. S. Umimoto of the Special Branch was on general observation duty. Nothing of an untoward nature occurred.

Officer i/c Special Branch.
（签名：D. S. Umimoto）

Subject (in full) Final Festival in connection with the installation ceremony at
Shanghai Shrine, Kiangwan Road.

Made by and Forwarded by D.S.I. White.

Sir,

At 9:00a.m. the 3/11/33, Mr. Ishii, Japanese Consul-General, Shrine
Committee members and representatives of the Japanese communal organ-
isations worshipped at the Shanghai Shrine.

Immediately after the termination of the aforesaid ceremony,
Vice-Admiral Imamura, Commander-in-Chief 3rd. Japanese Fleet, and Staff
Officers worshipped at the shrine and on the termination of the ser-
vice, proceeded to Hongkew Park to view the athletic meeting of the
personnel of the 3rd. Fleet.

Commencing from 12:20p.m. a series of entertains were held
in Hongkew Park, Japanese Naval Barracks and in the grounds of the
Shanghai Shrine. These various entertainments terminated at about
4:00p.m.

Between 7/8:30p.m. a cinema entertainment was held in the
grounds of the Shanghai Shrine.

At all ceremonies and entertainments, Municipal Police
functioned with the co-operation of the Japanese Consular Police.
No untoward incident occurred during the day's ceremonies and fest-
ivities.

I am, Sir,

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT

Subject (in full) Festival of the Shanghai Jinsha Shrine held in Hongkew Park
on November 1.

Made by D. S. Umemoto. Forwarded by [Signature]

The first grand festival in connection with the Shanghai
Jinsha Shrine, which was recently constructed in Kiangwan Road,
was held in Hongkew Park by the Japanese community at 1.00 p.m.
November 1.

The following functions were carried out:-
Games: Students of various Japanese schools participated
in the games which terminated at 3.10 p.m.
Jujitsu: An exhibition of jujitsu by members of the Japanese
Naval Landing Party, the Shobukai and the Tung Wen
College commenced at 1 p.m. and ended at 4 p.m.
Fencing: An exhibition of fencing by members of the Landing
Party, the Shobukai and the Tung Wen College
commenced at 1.00 p.m. and terminated at 4.30 p.m.
Archery: An exhibition of this art commenced at 2 p.m. and
terminated at 5.15 p.m.

Some 4,000 persons were present at the park and special
precautionary measures were adopted by a number of Police Officers
from Dixwell Road Station and the Reserve Unit in conjunction
with the local Japanese Consular Police. D. S. Umemoto of the
Special Branch was present on general observation duty. No
untoward incidents occurred.

The second day of the grand festival will be observed at
the Shanghai Shrine, Kiangwan Road, from 9 a.m. November 2.

[Signature]
D. S.

Officer i/c Special Branch

Sir,
At 3:30 a.m. the 1/11/33, representatives of Japanese communal
organisations of Shanghai visited the Shanghai Shrine, Jiangwan Road,
to worship and participate in the festivities.
At 10/30 a.m. Vice Admiral Imamura, Commander-in-Chief,
Japanese 3rd. Fleet, and one Battalion of the Japanese Naval Landing
Party visited the shrine to worship.
On the termination of the services held for the Naval Forces
about 1,000 Japanese School children visited the shrine and worship-

to the Japanese public.

Japanese community and members of the Japanese Naval Forces in
Hongkew Park. The meeting terminated at 5:00 p.m.

meeting in Hongkew Park, a party of police from Dixwell Road Station
Reserve Unit(E) and 3 Japanese Detectives from Hongkew
Station functioned in the locality in conjunction with the Japanese
Consular Police; No untoward incident occurred.

At 7 p.m. October 31, a procession of motor-cars conveying the "Spirit" of the Shanghai Jinsha Shrine and the Shokonsha Shrine, Kiangwan Road, under escort of the Municipal Police left the Japanese Consulate-General, Whangpoo Road, and proceeded to the shrine, arriving there at 7.30 p.m.

page_data.en:
October 31, 1933.
Festival of the Shanghai Shrine.

The "Divine Spirit" of the Shanghai Jinsha, which will
be consecrated in the recently erected Japanese Shanghai Shrine
at Kiangwan Road on October 31, was brought to Shanghai in the
care of Mr. Yasui, President of the local Japanese Residents'
Corporation, on the s.s. Shanghai Maru which berthed at the
N.Y.K. Wayside Wharf at 3.15 p.m. October 28, 1933. The "Spirit"
was conveyed from the vessel to the Japanese Consulate-General.

The "Divine Spirit" of the Shanghai Shrine will be removed
from the Japanese Consulate-General to the Shanghai Shrine, Kiang-
wan Road, at 7 p.m. October 31. It has been decided that
the vehicles shall proceed in the following order by way of
Whangpoo, Astor, Tiendong, Miller, Mingchen, Woosung, Yalu,
Haining, North Szechuen and Kiangwan Roads:-

Motor car escort (S.M.P.)
2 motor cycles (Naval Landing Party)
Motor car (Shinto priests)
Motor car (Spirit of the Shanghai Jinsha Shrine)
2 motor cycles (Naval Landing Party)
Motor car (Chairman of the Festival Committee)
Motor car (Spirit of the Shokonsha Shrine)
2 motor cycles (Naval Landing Party)
Motor car (Representatives of the Military)
Motor car (Members of the Festival Committee)
Motor car (Japanese Consular Police)
Motor car (S.M.P.)

The following programme of the festival on November 1, 2 and 3
has been arranged in the course of several meetings held by
members of the Festival Committee during the past ten days :-

November 1st.
8 a.m. Committee members will assemble at the office of the
Shrine.
8.30 a.m. to 10.30 a.m. Ceremony will be solemnized. After
the ceremony the public will be ordered to leave the
shrine. Vice Admiral Imamura, Commander-in-Chief of the
Third Fleet will then officially visit and worship
at the Shokonsha Shrine, following which a battalion
of the Naval Landing Party will pay their respects to
the Shanghai Shrine and the Shokonsha Shrine. Students
of the various schools will also visit the Shrine.
1 p.m. Athletic exercises and other games will be held by
students of various Japanese schools in Hongkew Park.
Exhibitions of jujitsu, fencing and archery will
be carried out in the park by officers and men of the
Third Fleet and the Naval Landing Party, students
of the Tung Wen College, members of the Shobukai
and the Ex-Service Men's Association.
page_data.zh:
1933年10月31日。
上海神社祭典。

将于10月31日在江湾路新建成的日本上海神社内举行奉安典礼的上海金刀比罗（Jinsha）“御灵”，由当地日本居留民团团长安井先生负责护送，乘“上海丸”轮于1933年10月28日下午3时15分抵靠日本邮船会社（N.Y.K.）外摆渡码头后运抵上海。“御灵”随后从船上被护送至日本总领事馆。

上海神社的“御灵”将于10月31日晚7时从日本总领事馆移往江湾路的上海神社。已决定车辆按以下顺序，经由黄浦路、阿斯特路（Astor Road）、天潼路、密勒路（Miller Road）、明尘路（Mingchen Road）、吴淞路、鸭绿江路、海宁路、北四川路和江湾路行进：-

警车护卫队（工部局警务处）
2辆摩托车（海军陆战队）

October 21, 1933. Morning Translation 20/10/33

MISCELLANEOUS.
NIPPO.

TWO JAPANESE CHILDREN INJURED
BY BOMB EXPLOSION.

At about 1.30 p.m. yesterday a bomb exploded at the entrance of the N.W.K. Cotton Mill quarters on Macao Road and injured two Japanese children named Y. Furuta and Y. Ichimyo; both 8 years old, son of an N.W.K. employees.
Both children were immediately removed to Hospital, one was detained with serious injuries, while the other was released after receiving treatment for a slight injury to the knee
It appears that the bomb was found by the children outside the quarters and exploded while they were playing with it. It is believed that the bomb is a relic of the fighting last years.

D 5032

With reference to the arrival of the "divine spirits" under the care of Mr. Yasui, on the S.S. Shanghai Maru during the afternoon of October 22, the following will provide an escort from the N.Y.K. wharf to the Japanese Consulate.

12. 1 motor car for S.M.P. officers.
The route of the procession will be Yangtszepoo, Broadway, Astor and Whangpoo Rds to the Japanese Consulate.

MAI NICHI.

COUNTERFEIT NOTE PASSED BY JAPANESE.

At about 10 p.m. October 19, a Japanes youth, age about 31, height about 5', visited the Japanese Cafe at 389 Jeukon Rd where he ordered a meal and afterwards a $5 note on the central Bank of China to pay the account of $ 4.60 he then left the cafe, later it was discovered the note was a f one.

杂项。
《日日新闻》。

两名日本儿童
因炸弹爆炸受伤。

昨日下午约1时30分，一枚炸弹在澳门路西北纺织厂（N.W.K. Cotton Mill）宿舍入口处爆炸，炸伤了两名名为 Y. Furuta 和 Y. Ichimyo 的日本儿童；两人均为8岁，系西北纺织厂员工之子。
两名儿童随即被送往医院，其中一人因伤势严重被留院治疗，另一人在接受膝盖轻微伤治疗后获释。
据悉，炸弹是孩子们在宿舍外发现并在玩耍时爆炸的。据信该炸弹是去年战斗遗留之物。

11. 日本领事警察汽车1辆，
12. 工部局警务处警官汽车1辆。
游行路线将为杨树浦路、百老汇路、阿斯特路和黄浦路，直至日本领事馆。

《每日新闻》。

日本人使用假钞。

10月19日晚约10时，一名约31岁、身高约5英尺的日本青年前往九江路389号的日本咖啡馆，点餐后使用一张面值5元的中央银行钞票支付4.60元的账目，随后离开咖啡馆。后经发现该钞票为假币。

Date October 23, 1933.

Subject (in full) Arrival of the "Divine Spirit" of the Japanese Shanghai Shrine.

Made by D.S. Pitta Forwarded by [Signature]

The "Divine Spirit" of the Shanghai Jinsha, which will
be consecrated in the recently erected Japanese Shanghai Shrine
at Kiangwan Road on October 31, was brought to Shanghai in the
care of Mr. Yasui, President of the local Japanese Residents'
Corporation, on the s.s. "Shanghai Maru", which berthed at the
N.Y.K. Wayside Wharf at 3.15 p.m. October 22, 1933.
The "Spirit" was conveyed from the vessel to the Japanese
Consulate-General, Whangpoo Road, by Mr. Ishii, Japanese Consul-
General and Rear-Admiral Sugisaka, Commander of the Japanese
Naval Landing Party. Some 2000 representatives of various
local Japanese public bodies were present in the compound of
the wharf to pay their respects to the Shinto "Spirit."
Special precautionary measures were adopted by the
Municipal Police in conjunction with the Japanese authorities
at the wharf and along the route to the Japanese Consulate-
General. An escort was provided by the Reserve Unit, whilst
detectives from Hongkew and Wayside stations were in attendance.
D.S. Pitts and D.S. Umemoto of the Special Branch carried out
general observation work but nothing of an untoward nature
transpired.

[Signature: Da. Pitts]
D. S.

Officer i/c Special Branch.
[Signature]

将于10月31日在江湾路新建成的日本上海神社内举行奉安典礼的上海金刀比罗“御灵”，由当地日本居留民团团长安井先生负责护送，乘“上海丸”轮于1933年10月22日下午3时15分抵靠日本邮船会社外摆渡码头后运抵上海。“御灵”随后由日本总领事石井先生和日本海军陆战队指挥官杉坂少将从船上护送至黄浦路的日本总领事馆。约有2000名当地各日本公共团体代表在码头院内列席，向神道“御灵”致敬。
工部局警务处与日本当局在码头及通往日本总领事馆的沿途采取了特别的预防措施。后备队提供了护卫，而虹口和外摆渡分站的侦探也在场执勤。特别支部的 D.S. Pitts 和 D.S. Umemoto 执行了一般观察任务，但未发生任何异常事件。

Afternoon Translation.

NICHI NICHI
MAI NICHI.
NIPPO.

FESTIVAL OF THE "SHANGHAI SHRINE"

Mr Yasui, president of the Japanese Residents Corporation has left for Japan in connection with the Shinto religious ceremonial of receiving the "divine spirit" on behalf of the Shanghai Shrine and the Shokonsha Shrine on Kiangwan Road. He will leave Kobe on October 20 on board the N.Y.K. steamer "Shanghai Maru" which is due to arrive here on October 22.

Upon its arrival, Mr Ishii, Consul General, Rear Admiral Sugisaka and senior members of the Japanese Residents Corporation and members of the committee for the Festival of the Shanghai Shrine, will remove the "divine spirits" to the Japanese consulate

In the compound, the Japanese Consular Police, Naval Landing Party, Gendarmerie, S.V.C. Japanese branch, S.M.P. Japanese Special Branch, Ex-service men, and Japanese boy scouts will form a guard. and S.M.P. and Naval Landing Party motor cycles will form an escort on the way to the Japanese Consulate.

All exservice men and street unions are requested to bring flags to the wharf.

MAI NICHI.

The Divine Spirit of the Shanghai Shrine and the Shokonsha
Shrine, Kiangwan Road, will arrive in Shanghai under the care of

the s.s. "Shanghai Maru", which is scheduled to berth at the
I.K.M. Quayside Pier during the afternoon of October 21.

Upon its arrival Mr. Ishii, Consul-General, Rear-Admiral
Sakamoto, Commander of the Japanese Naval Landing Party, senior
members of the Japanese Residents Association and several members
of the Committee for the Festival of the Shanghai Shrine, will
board the vessel and remove the spirit to the Japanese Consulate-
General, Whangpoo Road, by way of Yuenhszepoo Road, Broadway,
Astor and Whangpoo Roads.

Shrine, which is presided over by Mr. Ishii, Consul-General, that
precautionary measures be adopted by the Municipal Police in
conjunction with the Japanese Authorities both on the wharf and
along the route to be followed. A Police escort is also requested.

I forward herewith a plan showing precautionary measures
which will be adopted by the Authorities and the proceedings
to be observed at the wharf on October 22.

At 7.00 p.m. October 31, the spirit will be removed from
the Japanese Consulate-General, Whangpoo Road, to the Shanghai
Shrine, Kiangwan Road, by way of the following route:-

Whangpoo, Astor, Tienlong, Miller, Mingshong, Woosung, Yalu,
Haining, North Szechuen and Kiangwan Roads.

A detachment of the Japanese Naval Landing Party, teachers and
senior students of various Japanese schools and members of other
public bodies will assemble in Kiangwan Road awaiting its arrival.

由总领事石井先生主持的神社祭典委员会请求，工部局警务处与日本当局在码头及沿途路线采取预防措施。此外，还请求提供警察护卫。

现随函附上一张图表，显示当局将于10月22日在码头采取的预防措施及进行的程序。

10月31日晚7时，御神灵将从黄浦路的日本总领事馆移出，经以下路线送往江湾路的上海神社：

黄浦路、阿斯特路、天潼路、密勒路、明宏路、吴淞路、鸭绿江路、海宁路、北四川路和江湾路。

日本海军陆战队的一支分队、各日本学校的教师和高年级学生以及其他公共团体的成员将在江湾路集合，等候御神灵到达。在举行奉安典礼期间

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT
File No.
Date September 18th '33

Subject (in full) Inauguration of Japanese Shrine Ceremony

Made by D.S. Jones Forwarded by [Signature]

The ceremony in connection with the inauguration of the
new Shinto shrine in the Japanese garden opposite the new
barracks of the Japanese marines in Kiangwan Road began at
about 10 a.m. on September 17. Among the Japanese notabilities
who attended the function were Vice -Admiral Sugisaka, Officer
Commanding the Japanese Naval Landing Party, and Consul-General
Ishii. Altogether there must have been at least 3,000 Japanese
men, women and children present. The ceremony, which passed
off without anything untoward happening, concluded with the
hoisting into position of the last wooden beam to be secured
to the structure and the throwing of huge quantities of rice
cakes and other confections to the assembled multitude.

At 11.40 a.m. the crowd began to disperse, the people
returning quietly homeward.

Except for a mere handful of Chinese females, who appeared
to be there in the capacity of amahs to Japanese children, there
were no Chinese in evidence. Outside on the pavement a few
passers-by would pause awhile to see what was going on before
proceeding on their way.

The following members of the Special saw the function
through :

D.S. Jones, D.S. Kobayashi, D.S. Kim, C.D.S. 96,
Havildar Basant Singh and Dulla Singh.

[Signature]
D.S.

Officer i/c Special Branch

Commr. of Police.
Sir:
Information.
[Signature]
SEP 18 1933 O. i/c S. B.

日期：1933年9月18日

主题（全称）：日本神社落成典礼

撰写人：D.S. Jones 转呈人：[签名]

与江湾路日本海军陆战队新营房对面日本花园内新建神道教神社落成有关的典礼，于9月17日上午10时左右开始。出席该活动的日本名流包括日本海军陆战队指挥官杉坂少将和总领事石井。在场的日本男女老少至少有3000人。典礼过程顺利，未发生任何意外，最后以将最后一根木梁吊装到位固定于建筑结构上，并向聚集的人群抛洒大量年糕和其他糕点而告终。

上午11时40分，人群开始散去，人们安静地回家。

除了少数几名似乎是作为日本儿童保姆的中国女性外，现场没有发现其他中国人。在外面的人行道上，少数路人会驻足片刻观看正在发生的事情，然后继续前行。

特别处的下列成员全程监视了该活动：

D.S. Jones, D.S. Kobayashi, D.S. Kim, C.D.S. 96,
印籍警长 Basant Singh 和 Dulla Singh。

[签名]
D.S.

特别处主管警官

情报。

Subject (in full) Ceremony of laying of foundation stone in connection with shrine
dedicated Japanese combatants killed in Sino-Japanese hostilities.

Made by and Forwarded by D.S.I. White.

Sir,

Between 10:00a.m. and 10:30a.m. the 25/6/33, the Japanese Consul-
General, Mr. Ishii, in conjunction with Japanese military and naval
officials officiate at the laying of a stone in connection with
the building of a shrine dedicated to combatants of the Japanese
Forces who were killed in the Sino Japanese hostilities of last
year. The shrine is located on Kiangwan Road opposite the new
building of the Japanese Special Naval Landing Party Headquarters.
The Officer-in-Charge of District with a party of police was in
attendance and the Japanese Consular Police also functioned at the
ceremony. Nothing of an untoward nature occurred during the ceremony.
